# Analyze late-season patterns (D170-D213) to understand what's happening now and plan next season
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

trips = tables['trips']

# Filter season 6 data from d170 onwards
s6_late = trips[(trips['fish_date_season'] == 6) & (trips['fish_date_doy'] >= 170)].copy()

# Calculate daily averages by class
daily_by_class = s6_late.groupby(['fish_date_doy', 'cls']).agg({
    'yt': 'sum',
    'anglers': 'sum',
    'landing': 'count'
}).reset_index()

daily_by_class['yt_per_angler'] = daily_by_class['yt'] / daily_by_class['anglers']

# Summary by class for entire period
class_summary = s6_late.groupby('cls').agg({
    'yt': 'sum',
    'anglers': 'sum',
    'landing': 'count'
}).reset_index()
class_summary['yt_per_angler'] = class_summary['yt'] / class_summary['anglers']
class_summary = class_summary.sort_values('yt_per_angler', ascending=False)

print("=== SEASON 6 D170-D213 SUMMARY ===")
print("\nClass Performance:")
print(class_summary[['cls', 'yt', 'anglers', 'yt_per_angler', 'landing']].to_string(index=False))

# Look at last 20 days more closely
recent_20 = daily_by_class[daily_by_class['fish_date_doy'] >= 193].copy()
print(f"\n=== LAST 20 DAYS (D193-D213) ===")
print(f"Hot days (>1.0 yt/angler): {len(recent_20[recent_20['yt_per_angler'] > 1.0])}")
print("\nBest recent runs:")
top_recent = recent_20.nlargest(10, 'yt_per_angler')[['fish_date_doy', 'cls', 'yt', 'anglers', 'yt_per_angler']]
print(top_recent.to_string(index=False))

# Check if there's a pattern emerging
print("\n=== PATTERN CHECK D170-D213 ===")
for doy in sorted(daily_by_class['fish_date_doy'].unique())[-20:]:

    print(f"D{doy}: max {max_rate:.3f} yt/angler ({best_class})")
